claimed_purpose.text: The product exposes memory card types for structured memory extraction and storage.
Portable AI memory system giving users control over persistent knowledge
Memvid is described as providing portable, single-file AI memory

mechanisms.text: commit() is a public method on the Memvid wrapper intended to flush pending writes to disk, but the internal _MemvidCore delegation target does not implement it, causing silent data loss
Frames (units of stored content) are written via put_bytes / put_bytes_with_options / put_with_embedding and committed to a .mv2 file; the store persists across open/close cycles.
MemoryCards are curated per-entity slot/value pairs (not a message log); each card has a slot name, a value, and a source_frame_id — these are the persisted memory unit
get_current_memory retrieves the single current value for a named slot on a named entity, implying supersession: only one value per (entity, slot) is 'current'
Memory persisted in a single portable file format (.mv2) containing raw data, embeddings, hybrid search indexes, and a crash-safe write-ahead log
The stats command reads and displays ticket metadata and capacity usage, but ticket enforcement at write time may follow a different code path.
Unverified tickets are flagged in stats output, suggesting a cloud verification step may be required for tickets to be honoured at write time.
The WAL corruption is durable on disk, not an in-memory artifact — reopening the store hits the same checksum mismatch while scanning records.
Model binding is persistent: index is locked to a specific embedding model; mismatches fail fast to prevent mixing embeddings across sessions
ACL types include tenant_id, principal, role, and resource_id keys, indicating per-tenant and per-principal isolation at the frame level.
frame_context performs keyword match counting by lowercasing document content and matching query words against it, used during retrieval
Memory is stored as append-only, immutable Smart Frames with timestamps, checksums, and metadata; existing frames are never modified
EnrichmentEngine extracts memory cards from frames during ingestion; EnrichmentRecord and EnrichmentManifest track enrichment state.
SearchRequest carries optional temporal and as_of_frame / as_of_ts fields, indicating the store supports point-in-time retrieval
Frames are the unit of indexed storage; each frame stores content text, timestamp, frame_id, tags, labels, track, and uri fields
The current write path is limited to a single writer at a time, blocking concurrent multi-agent writes to the same memory file.
MemoryCard and associated builder types represent curated, structured memory extraction distinct from the raw frame/WAL log.
Memory is stored in a single mv2 file containing an index and a time index, with configurable byte size limits for each
All agent sessions (main agent, subagents, background processes) share a single memory file for both reads and writes.
Hybrid retrieval combines graph traversal and vector/lex search via GraphMatcher, QueryPlanner, and hybrid_search.
Automatic Subject-Predicate-Object (SPO) triplet extraction is performed during ingestion via TripletExtractor.
Vector documents are stored as (frame_id, embedding) pairs and serialized to bytes via bincode for persistence.
retrieve: SearchRequest with query, top_k, and snippet_chars fields; returns ranked hits with text and title
Isolation is at the capsule (file) level; capsules are self-contained with rules and expiry (.mv2 format)
Adaptive retrieval provides dynamic result-set sizing with configurable cutoff strategies.
Single portable file that code can read, append to, and update across interactions
The put() API writes a memory frame with title, label, text, and tags fields.
Smart Recall targets sub-5ms local memory access with predictive caching
create() and use() are the open/reopen API surface for .mv2 store files
Append-only frame architecture for crash safety and time-travel queries

ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Memvid is a portable AI memory system with a single-file architecture (.mv2)
ledger.quote: Welcome to Memvid, the portable AI memory system that puts you in control.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The .mv2 store persists documents, vector embeddings, BM25 and vector indices, a time index, and a WAL in a single file
ledger.quote: Every `.mv2` file is completely self-contained: Your data: Documents, text, images, audio, videos; Embeddings: Vector representations for semantic search; Indices: BM25 lexical index and vector index; Time index: Temporal ordering for timeline queries; Write-ahead log: Crash-safe transaction logging
ledger.locator: What Makes Memvid Different / Single-File Architecture
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Retrieval supports three modes: hybrid (auto), lexical (BM25), and semantic (vector)
ledger.quote:
# Hybrid search (recommended)
memvid find knowledge.mv2 --query "user authentication" --mode auto
# Lexical search - exact keyword matching
memvid find knowledge.mv2 --query "authentication" --mode lex
# Semantic search - conceptual understanding
memvid find knowledge.mv2 --query "how do users log in" --mode sem
ledger.locator: What Makes Memvid Different / Hybrid Search Engine
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Storage uses append-only frame architecture inspired by video formats, enabling time-travel queries
ledger.quote: Frame Architecture: Video-inspired append-only storage for crash safety and time-travel queries
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Search over 50K documents completes in under 20ms; bulk ingestion exceeds 150 docs/sec; frame append is under 0.1ms
ledger.quote: Search (50K docs) < 20ms; Bulk ingestion 150+ docs/sec; Frame append < 0.1ms
ledger.locator: What Makes Memvid Different / Lightning Performance
ledger.label: inferred

No description of conflict/supersession behavior when correct() or enrich() are called on an existing frame — how the store resolves duplicate or contradictory facts is not stated.
No documentation on how the WAL is read back into retrieval context — whether scanning is sequential, indexed, or filtered — is present on this page.
Recovery or repair behavior after WAL checksum corruption is explicitly out of scope for this issue and not described.
